attribution.scope: First observed protection/component rejection on one API clock; not proof of an unexercised hardware bottleneck.

operatingHeadroom.scope: Validated local mixed-read operating target for this profile and duration; deployment sizing requires its own run.

attribution.clock: single API-process monotonic clock; first observed component rejection

capacity.guidance: The measured boundary includes existing IP/account/shop policy. Review the traffic distribution and rejection codes before changing quotas; more API instances alone do not establish a higher safe policy ceiling.
limitations: Single local API and owned PostgreSQL, four read workflows, three owner identities/shops and at most 48 loopback source IPs; not concurrent human-user capacity.
Short plateaus and inherited bucket history describe this exact ramp; they do not establish sustained throughput or statistically reliable p99 at low rates.
A confirmation repeats the failing level in the same fixture; independent-run reproducibility and deployment-specific capacity remain separate checks.
Headroom is validated only for the recorded sustained duration, fixture and traffic distribution; not a deployment sizing or autoscaling threshold.
Owned PostgreSQL CPU is sampled from live process counters once per second; CPU between worker creation/exit and sampling can be missed. Realtime and WAN bottlenecks are outside this read profile.

monitoring.processScope: API and collector process; fixture generation shares this process during setup. Search clients run in a separate process.
monitoring.networkScope: Observed loopback HTTP socket bytes, including headers; not NIC/WAN or database protocol bandwidth.
